_comment: Test batteries: the integration suite partitioned by subsystem, one battery
per CI runner. THE single source — scripts/run_unittest_suite.py selects
files from it and .github/workflows/ci.yml builds its matrix from it, so a
battery is added in one place and both follow.
Batteries are semantic, not duration-balanced: 'networking' is far the largest and
sets the critical path. That is deliberate. A red job named 'networking' says what
broke without opening a log, and membership stays stable as tests are added,
so a battery's history stays comparable run to run — neither of which is true
of an i-of-N shard, where adding one test reshuffles every partition.
Every file under tests/ MUST appear in exactly one battery.
run_unittest_suite.py --verify-batteries enforces it and runs in the quality
gate; without it a newly added test could belong to no battery and silently
never run, which is the one failure mode a numeric shard cannot have.
needs_qemu=false marks a battery that runs without the emulation toolchain,
so CI can schedule it on a cheap fast job instead of paying for OVMF/QEMU.

batteries.name: boot-and-init
batteries.description: Boot chain, init, CLI and panic decoding: the system comes up and is usable.

batteries.name: scheduler-and-ipc
batteries.description: Scheduler, preemption, threading, IPC wakeup and shared-memory grants.

batteries.name: networking
batteries.description: Networking end to end: the virtio-net driver, net-stack, sockets, DNS and TLS.

batteries.name: graphics-and-vt
batteries.description: Graphics, virtual terminals and hardware input routing.

batteries.name: filesystem
batteries.description: Filesystem reads and writes through the FAT backend.

batteries.name: language-runtimes
batteries.description: One guest per supported source language boots and runs.

batteries.name: host-tools
batteries.description: Host tools, exercised directly. Boots nothing and needs no emulation.
